articles.title_original: Surface and Interface Engineering of MXenes Enables TCO‐Free Silicon Heterojunction Solar Cells
articles.title_en: MXene Surface Engineering Enables TCO-Free Silicon Heterojunction Solar Cells
articles.excerpt_original: ABSTRACT Indium tin oxide (ITO) remains the conventional transparent electrode in silicon heterojunction (SHJ) solar cells, yet its reliance on scarce indium raises concerns over cost and scalability. MXenes are solution‐processable and indium‐free, but have so far been confined to electrode roles rather than functioning as primary transparent electrodes that fully displace ITO, particularly on the optically demanding front side. Here we report a fully TCO‐free SHJ solar cell in which surface‐termination engineering enables Ti 3 C 2 T x MXene to act as the transparent electrode on both sides. Hydroxyl‐rich and oxygen‐terminated Ti 3 C 2 T x were synthesized for the front and rear contacts, respectively, with their work functions tuned for the required energy‐level alignment. A front MgF 2 antireflection coating and a rear Ti 3 C 2 T x /AgNW hybrid electrode offset the intrinsic optical losses and inter‐flake resistance of the MXene films. The optimized device reached an efficiency of 23.14%, comparable to a co‐processed, industrially relevant ITO reference. The performance was highly reproducible, with a relative standard deviation in efficiency below 1%, and the devices retained on average over 95% of their initial efficiency after 304 days of storage. These findings establish termination‐engineered MXenes as a credible transparent‐electrode option for next‐generation, indium‐free SHJ photovoltaics.
articles.summary_en: Researchers developed termination-engineered Ti₃C₂Tₓ MXene electrodes that replace indium tin oxide on both sides of silicon heterojunction solar cells. The optimized device achieved 23.14% efficiency and retained over 95% of its initial performance after 304 days, indicating a credible indium-free transparent-electrode route.

articles.title_original: Disclosing Trendson C(1s) Core-Level Binding Energiesof MXene Flakes: Metal, Size and Edge Effects
articles.title_en: DFT Study Maps C(1s) Binding-Energy Trends in MXene Flakes
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract The C(1s) core-level binding energies (CLBE) of realistic MXene finite systems were investigated using density functional theory (DFT). The ΔSCF approach was employed to explicitly account for final state effects. MXene flakes with M2CTx stoichiometry (M = Sc, Y, Ti, Zr, Hf, V, Nb, and Ta, where Tx denotes surface termination), consisting of 18 stoichiometric units, were constructed in both pristine (M2C)18 and O-functionalized (M2CO2)18 forms. CLBEs were computed for all C atoms in each flake using the PBE functional, which was found to correlate linearly with results from the more accurate hybrid PBE0 functional. An increase in CLBEs is observed across periods, driven by decreasing atomic radii and increasing metal electronegativity, whereas trends along groups follow a behavior similar to that of first ionization potentials. O-functionalized flakes exhibit higher CLBEs due to the electronegative effect and the structural distortion caused by the O termination. This enables a clear distinction between pristine and O-terminated materials in XPS spectra. In addition, the flake size effect on central carbons in (Ti2C)n and (Ti2CO2)n flakes, with n up to 216, is negligible, supporting the extrapolation of the present results for larger systems. Overall, the C(1s) XPS spectra of MXene flakes are expected to be centered around the CLBE of the central C atom, with peak widths determined by the difference between the maximum and minimum CLBE values.
articles.summary_en: Density functional theory calculations show that MXene C(1s) core-level binding energies vary with metal identity, flake size, and oxygen termination. The results support distinguishing pristine and O-terminated MXenes through XPS analysis and extrapolating central-carbon values to larger flakes.

articles.title_original: Second order unfitted ghost-FEM for elliptic interface problems with applications to low-dimensional semiconductor devices
articles.title_en: Ghost-FEM Method Advances Graphene Transistor Simulation
articles.excerpt_original: We develop an unfitted ghost finite element method for elliptic interface problems with discontinuous diffusion coefficients and apply it to the electrostatic simulation of low-dimensional semiconductor devices. The proposed approach is based on a fixed Cartesian grid and represents the geometry by level-set functions, avoiding mesh generation and remeshing even in the presence of interfaces. A snapping-back-to-grid strategy is used to control the small-cut-cell issue, while interface conditions are weakly enforced by a symmetric Nitsche formulation. The method is first validated on benchmark elliptic interface problems with different geometries and coefficient jumps, showing second-order accuracy for the solution and first-order accuracy for its gradient. As an application, we consider a graphene field-effect transistor described by a self-consistent drift-diffusion-Poisson model. The electrostatic potential is computed in a two-dimensional oxide/graphene/oxide structure, while charge transport in the graphene layer is modeled by one-dimensional bipolar drift-diffusion equations in the degenerate case and by including a field-dependent mobility model. The coupled nonlinear system is solved by a damped fixed-point iteration combined with a domain-decomposition treatment of the three-layer geometry. Numerical simulations reproduce transfer characteristics with a clear transition from an OFF state to an ON state and show the influence of the gate voltage on the two-dimensional electrostatic potential. The results also indicate that the effective thickness and discretization of the graphene layer affect the transverse potential profile, supporting the use of a full two-dimensional electrostatic description with explicit oxide/graphene interface conditions.
articles.summary_en: Researchers developed a second-order unfitted ghost finite element method for elliptic interface problems and applied it to self-consistent electrostatic and transport modeling of graphene field-effect transistors. Simulations captured gate-controlled OFF-to-ON behavior and showed that graphene thickness and discretization affect potential profiles, supporting explicit two-dimensional interface modeling.

articles.title_original: Machine-Learning-Driven Investigation of Dopant-Induced Modulation of Electronic Properties in Two-Dimensional SnO
articles.title_en: Machine Learning Maps Dopant-Tunable Properties of 2D SnO
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract Machine learning has become an effective tool for accelerating materials discovery by&#xD;predicting material properties with far lower computational cost than exhaustive&#xD;first-principles calculations. However, its application to dopant engineering in&#xD;two-dimensional (2D) oxide semiconductors remains relatively unexplored. In this work,&#xD;we combine supervised machine learning with density functional theory (DFT)-derived&#xD;data from the Materials Project database to predict the electronic, thermodynamic,&#xD;transport, and optical properties of undoped and doped 2D tin monoxide (SnO). Several&#xD;supervised regression algorithms are evaluated for predicting the band gap, formation&#xD;energy, carrier mobility, electrical conductivity, and optical absorption coefficient. Among&#xD;the models considered, Gradient Boosting Regression provides the highest predictive&#xD;accuracy and consistently reproduces the complex structure–property relationships of both&#xD;undoped and doped systems. Feature-importance analysis reveals that electronic band&#xD;descriptors, particularly band width, followed by band asymmetry and electronic&#xD;anisotropy, are the primary factors governing band-gap prediction, while structural&#xD;descriptors provide complementary contributions. The predictions indicate that monolayer&#xD;SnO has a wider band gap, slightly higher formation energy, and higher carrier mobility&#xD;than bulk SnO due to quantum confinement. Mg and Zn substitution allow systematic&#xD;tuning of the material properties over a moderate concentration range. The band gap&#xD;changes only slightly with doping, while Mg incorporation is thermodynamically more&#xD;favorable than Zn, whos
articles.summary_en: Researchers combined supervised machine learning with density-functional-theory data to predict electronic, thermodynamic, transport, and optical properties of two-dimensional tin monoxide. The analysis indicates that monolayer SnO offers higher carrier mobility than bulk material, while magnesium and zinc substitution enable moderate property tuning, with magnesium being more thermodynamically favorable.

articles.title_original: Emergence of resonating valence-bond correlations in stretched graphene
articles.title_en: Stretched graphene exhibits resonating valence-bond correlations
articles.summary_en: APS reports the emergence of resonating valence-bond correlations in graphene under mechanical strain. The finding advances fundamental understanding of strain-tuned electronic states, but no immediate commercial application is identified.

articles.title_original: Single-gate graphene thermopiles enabled by locally Al-modified graphene legs on PET substrates
articles.title_en: Single-Gate Graphene Thermopiles with Locally Aluminum-Modified Legs
articles.excerpt_original: We report a simplified graphene thermopile architecture fabricated on PET substrates. Conventional single-material graphene thermopiles typically require independent electrostatic control of the two thermoelectric legs, increasing both fabrication complexity and device footprint. Here, one graphene leg is locally modified by an Al overlayer, while the overall carrier density is tuned using a single global ionic-liquid gate. As a reference, graphene/Au thermopiles exhibit the expected linear scaling of thermovoltage with the number of thermocouples, but their output remains limited by the small thermopower of Au. In contrast, the Al-covered graphene leg generates a large, weakly gate-dependent negative thermovoltage contribution while preserving graphene-dominated transport, thereby enhancing the thermoelectric contrast with the uncovered graphene leg. Consequently, graphene/Al-covered graphene thermopiles exhibit a substantially higher output voltage, which increases approximately linearly with thermocouple number and surpasses that of the graphene/Au reference structure. These results establish local Al-induced electronic modification as a simple and scalable strategy for realizing graphene thermopiles without multiple local gates, providing a device platform compatible with flexible and transparent polymer substrates.
articles.summary_en: Researchers developed graphene thermopiles on flexible PET substrates using a local aluminum overlayer and a single global ionic-liquid gate. The architecture increases thermovoltage versus graphene/gold references while reducing fabrication complexity and device footprint, supporting scalable flexible thermoelectric devices.

articles.title_original: Polarization engineered all 2D Graphene/Ferroelectric hybrid for persistence-free photoresponse
articles.title_en: Graphene–3R-MoS₂ photodetector delivers fast, persistence-free photoresponse
articles.excerpt_original: Graphene-based van der Waals hybrid photodetectors typically work on trap-mediated photogating mechanism, exhibiting high sensitivity, but under-perform in the fast detection of repetitive optical signals. Designing photodetectors that are simultaneously fast and highly sensitive has therefore remained difficult. In this work, we realize both attributes by integrating atomically thin sliding ferroelectrics in the design architecture, thereby uniting semiconducting properties with intrinsic polarization fields capable of efficiently governing interfacial photocarrier dynamics. We report a bilayer graphene-bilayer MoS2 (with MoS2 in a rhombohedrally stacked (3R) configuration) van der Waals photodetector with edge-contacted dual-gated field-effect transistor architecture. The photo-induced modulation in spontaneous out-of-plane polarization of 3R-MoS2 and selective confinement of charge carriers in bilayer graphene under an out-of-plane displacement field results in a tunable persistence-free photoresponse. Here, the photoinduced polarization change in 3R-MoS2 produces an optically controlled gating effect that alters the electrostatic environment of bilayer graphene, resulting in a temperature-independent photoresponse with rapid response times of the order of 10's of milliseconds (limited by the measurement instrument). We demonstrate reproducible detection of optical signals and examine the photon-counting resolution of this structure in high-sensitivity regimes, where we determine its internal quantum efficiency to be 10 percent with minimum detectable photon number of 31 in single shot measurements. This work highlights the functionality of 3R-MoS2 in manipulating the interfacial charge dynamics and establishes the hybrid of graphene and ferroelectric 3R-MoS2 as a pr
articles.summary_en: Researchers developed a bilayer graphene/ferroelectric 3R-MoS₂ photodetector that combines high sensitivity with rapid, persistence-free detection of repetitive optical signals. The device achieved response times on the order of tens of milliseconds, 10% internal quantum efficiency, and single-shot detection of as few as 31 photons.

articles.title_original: Interfacial Engineering of Printable MOF/MXene Heterostructured Inks for High‐Performance Wearable Ammonia Sensors
articles.title_en: Printable MOF/MXene Inks Enable Wearable Ammonia Sensing
articles.excerpt_original: ABSTRACT Precise molecular recognition and efficient signal transduction are pivotal for next‐generation wearable health‐monitoring platforms, particularly for detecting breath biomarkers like ammonia (NH 3 ) that indicate renal or hepatic distress. However, achieving high‐selectivity NH 3 sensing in complex, trace‐level environments is often hindered by low sensitivity. Herein, we report a sustainable, low‐temperature strategy for the synthesis of printable and textile‐compatible MOF/MXene heterostructured inks tailored for high‐performance NH 3 sensing. We demonstrate that precise interfacial engineering and functional group alignment between the MXene and MOF phases trigger a robust synergistic effect, significantly accelerating charge‐transfer kinetics. The resulting sensor achieves an extraordinary detection limit of 3 ppb, markedly outperforming current state‐of‐the‐art benchmarks. For practical application, the sensing unit was integrated into a custom wearable wristband equipped with real‐time signal processing and wireless transmission modules, exhibiting sensing capabilities on par with commercial sensors. This tailored synthesis strategy, coupled with systematic platform integration, enables non‐invasive monitoring of trace NH 3 in human breath. This synergy provides a viable approach for the early screening of chronic kidney disease (CKD) while expanding the horizons for functional material development in next‐generation intelligent wearable diagnostics.
articles.summary_en: Researchers developed textile-compatible MOF/MXene heterostructured inks for wearable ammonia sensors, reporting a 3 ppb detection limit. Integrated into a wireless wristband, the platform supports real-time breath monitoring and potential early screening for chronic kidney disease.

articles.title_original: Effect of h-BN nanoparticles and dimple textures on the friction and wear performance of the marine grade stainless steel
articles.title_en: h-BN nanoparticles and surface dimples improve marine steel wear resistance
articles.excerpt_original: Surface texturing has emerged as an effective strategy to improve the tribological performance of sliding components. This study examines the synergistic influence of micro-dimple textures and hexagonal boron nitride (h-BN) solid lubricant on the tribological behavior of marine-grade steel (AISI 316 L). Three textured surfaces with dimple densities of 5% (T-5), 9% (T-9), and 20% (T-20) were investigated. Among them, T-20 exhibited the highest oil spreading ability, with a contact angle of 36.1°, compared to 76.08° for the untextured surface (T-0). Under dry sliding conditions, the wear coefficient showed significant reductions compared to T-0: 52.7% for T-5, 44.1% for T-9, and 66.7% for T-20. In lubricated conditions, the T-20 surface combined with h-BN nanoparticles (T-20-L-BN) demonstrated the lowest average wear coefficient among all textured surfaces, achieving an impressive 97.3% reduction compared to T-0. The enhanced tribological performance is attributed to the synergistic effect of dimple textures and h-BN nanoparticles, where dimples improve lubricant retention and debris trapping, while h-BN facilitates the formation of a protective tribofilms. These results highlight that integrating optimized surface textures with solid lubricants significantly enhances wear resistance and friction behavior, offering promising applications in marine and engineering components.
articles.summary_en: Researchers found that combining micro-dimple textures with hexagonal boron nitride nanoparticles reduced the lubricated wear coefficient of AISI 316L stainless steel by 97.3%. The approach improves lubricant retention and debris trapping, suggesting potential for marine and engineering components.

articles.title_original: Impact of BGaN EBL on Non-Radiative Recombination and Carrier Transport in 266-nm AlGaN DUV Nanowire Lasers
articles.title_en: BGaN Electron-Blocking Layers Improve 266-nm AlGaN Nanowire Lasers
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract DUV laser diodes include continuous-wave lasing at around 270 nm, improved hole injection with transparent tunnel junctions, and lower threshold current density through improved waveguide and substrate design. Limitations of laser devices include electron leakage and an increase in threshold current. Electron blocking layers control electron leakage from the multi-quantum wells (MQWs) in ultraviolet nanowire laser diodes. In this work, a boron-based (BGaN/L1), (BGaN/L2) electron blocking layer and composition grading (60% 70%) AlGaN N-WG enhance carrier confinement in AlGaN DUV nanowire lasers and decrease electron leakage. Boron GaN composition grading WG increases the conduction band barrier, suppressing electron leakage from the MQWs, while reducing the valence band barrier to improve hole injection. Boron (BGaN/L1), (BGaN/L2) electron blocking layer combined with an optimized N-type waveguide significantly enhances device performance. Optical power is increased by 15.47%, and the gain is increased 16.9%. While the threshold voltage, threshold current, and Non-Radiative Recombination are reduced by 4.49%, 33.24%, and 24.50%, respectively, with an emission wavelength of 266 nm. These results show that boron electron blocking layers are an effective approach for improving the efficiency of AlGaN DUV nanowire lasers.
articles.summary_en: Researchers report that boron-containing GaN electron-blocking layers and graded AlGaN waveguides reduce electron leakage and improve hole injection in deep-ultraviolet nanowire lasers. The design increased optical power by 15.47% and reduced threshold current by 33.24% and non-radiative recombination by 24.50%.

articles.title_original: Anisotropic electron gas in a hyperbolic van der Waals material
articles.title_en: Raman spectroscopy reveals anisotropic electron gas in hyperbolic MoOCl2
articles.excerpt_original: Electron gases in low-dimensional materials exhibit unusual optical and electronic phenomena arising from reduced dimensionality and enhanced interactions. While such states are typically engineered in quantum-confined systems and heterostructures, they rarely occur in naturally existing materials. Hyperbolic materials provide a unique platform where extreme lattice anisotropy can give rise to unconventional electronic states and electron-phonon interactions, yet experimental probes of their underlying electron dynamics remain limited. Here, we show that angle-resolved polarized Raman spectroscopy reveals anisotropic electron-phonon coupling in MoOCl2, a naturally occurring hyperbolic material whose optical response originates from a highly anisotropic electron gas. Pronounced polarization-dependent Fano line shapes reveal coherent coupling between optical phonons and an anisotropic electronic continuum. A microscopic model quantitatively reproduces the Raman spectra and identifies a distinct spectroscopic fingerprint of the anisotropic electron gas. Excitation-energy- and thickness-dependent measurements further reveal a tunable continuum with weak interlayer coupling. Our results establish Raman spectroscopy as a sensitive probe of electron-phonon interactions in naturally hyperbolic materials and anisotropic electron gases. Low-dimensional electron gases can give rise to unusual light-matter interactions, but naturally occurring examples are rare. Here, the authors show that Raman spectroscopy reveals a unique fingerprint of the strongly anisotropic electron gas in the hyperbolic material MoOCl2 through its interaction with lattice vibrations.
articles.summary_en: Researchers report that polarized Raman spectroscopy can detect anisotropic electron–phonon coupling and an electronic continuum in naturally occurring hyperbolic MoOCl2. Thickness- and excitation-dependent measurements indicate a tunable continuum with weak interlayer coupling, positioning Raman spectroscopy as a probe of low-dimensional electronic behavior.

articles.title_original: Size-Dependent Band-Tail Localization in Oxide Semiconductors Revealed by Direct Density-of-States Mapping
articles.title_en: Direct DOS Mapping Reveals Size-Dependent Localization in Oxide Semiconductor TFTs
articles.excerpt_original: Disorder-induced localization is expected to become increasingly important as amorphous oxide semiconductor transistors are scaled toward low-dimensional channels, yet the electronic states responsible for this transport regime remain difficult to resolve experimentally. Here, we use a lock-in-based electric-field penetration technique to directly map the effective density of states (DOS) in In-based oxide semiconductor thin-film transistors (TFTs). The extracted quantum capacitance, carrier density, and chemical potential reveal a disorder-dominated transport regime in which band-tail states are not merely passive traps, but become screening-active and partially transport-active. Geometry-dependent DOS mapping shows an exponential suppression of the effective DOS with channel length, demonstrating size-dependent band-tail localization and providing a microscopic origin for a distinct localization-induced threshold-voltage roll-off mechanism. Temperature-dependent measurements show that the disorder-dominated DOS is strongly suppressed at low temperatures, while extended diffusive states remain nearly unchanged, confirming the localization origin. By tuning film thickness, O2 annealing, and In/Ga/Zn composition, we further demonstrate systematic suppression of disorder and effective-DOS localization. This work establishes direct DOS mapping as a device-level probe of localization physics and provides a pathway for engineering disorder in low-dimensional oxide semiconductor electronics.
articles.summary_en: Researchers directly mapped the density of states in indium-based oxide thin-film transistors, showing that band-tail states become screening- and partially transport-active as channel dimensions shrink. Film thickness, oxygen annealing, and In/Ga/Zn composition were identified as routes to suppress disorder and localization in low-dimensional oxide electronics.

articles.title_original: Stepwise growth of graphene on silicon carbide: Decoupling formation buffer layer from graphene growth
articles.title_en: Stepwise Process Enables Uniform Wafer-Scale Graphene Growth on Silicon Carbide
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract Epitaxial growth of graphene on silicon carbide (SiC) offers a promising route to high-quality and wafer-scale graphene directly on a wide bandgap semiconductor, eliminating transfer-induced contamination. Conventional growth, however, relies on extremely high temperatures that often provoke severe step bunching on the SiC surface, impairing graphene uniformity and device performance. To overcome this limitation, we present a stepwise growth strategy that exploits buffer-mediated kinetic control, with first-principles calculations confirming its thermodynamic feasibility. The process employs a carefully controlled two-stage temperature program. First, a continuous buffer layer is formed on SiC(0001) at a relatively low temperature. This layer acts as a diffusion barrier, confining sublimated Si atoms to step edges and suppressing terrace-scale atomic migration, thereby inhibiting giant step bunching and stabilizing the surface morphology. In the second stage, raising the temperature drives graphene growth. The pre-formed buffer layer serves as a carbon reservoir, delivering a uniform supply of precursors across terraces and enabling dual-site nucleation at both steps and terraces. This promotes rapid lateral expansion of monolayer graphene while further suppressing step bunching. Compared with conventional high-temperature direct growth, this stepwise approach substantially reduces giant step bunching, disrupts the step-edge-dominated nucleation paradigm, and yields more controllable nucleation alongside a stabilized surface morphology. As a result, large-area, uniform, and high-quality monolayer single-crystal graphene can be reliably obtained.
articles.summary_en: Researchers report a two-stage temperature process that forms a buffer layer before graphene growth, suppressing step bunching on silicon carbide. The approach enables more uniform, high-quality monolayer single-crystal graphene directly on a semiconductor substrate, potentially benefiting wafer-scale device fabrication.

articles.title_original: Engineering Dirac Cones in Graphene for Efficient Iodide Catalysis: Insights by Nanoscale Electrochemistry
articles.title_en: Engineering Graphene Dirac Cones Enhances Iodide Oxidation Catalysis
articles.excerpt_original: Advances in atomically thin two-dimensional materials have created new opportunities to regulate interfacial charge transfer and surface reactivity in electrocatalysis. Among anodic reactions relevant to sustainable energy conversion, the iodide oxidation reaction (IOR) has emerged as an attractive alternative to the oxygen evolution reaction because of its lower overpotential, faster kinetics, and simultaneous generation of value-added iodine species. Here, by using scanning electrochemical cell microscopy, we show that the electronic structure of graphene can be engineered to promote IOR through two experimentally distinct routes: electrostatic gating in monolayer graphene and twist-angle control in bilayer graphene. Gate-dependent measurements show that hole doping promotes iodide oxidation, whereas electron doping suppresses it, consistent with Fermi-level modulation of electron extraction from iodide. Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene (MATBG) exhibits a lower onset potential and stronger IOR response than monolayer and Bernal-stacked bilayer graphene. The enhanced activity of MATBG is associated with a moiré-reconstructed interfacial electronic environment that facilitates IOR. These results establish electronic-structure engineering of graphene as an effective strategy for regulating nanoscale iodide oxidation and highlight Dirac-cone engineering as a tunable platform for sustainable iodine redox electrochemistry.
articles.summary_en: Researchers used electrostatic gating and twist-angle control to tune graphene’s electronic structure for iodide oxidation. Hole-doped monolayer graphene and magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene showed stronger catalytic responses, highlighting moiré engineering as a route to iodine redox electrochemistry.

articles.title_original: Memory circuit elements for hardware security: a review from memristors to memcapacitors and meminductors
articles.title_en: Review assesses mem-elements for hardware security
articles.excerpt_original: The security of modern electronic systems is increasingly grounded in the physical properties of hardware, rather than on purely algorithmic assumptions. In this context, passive circuit elements with memory, commonly referred to as mem-elements, have emerged as promising candidates for implementing hardware-based security primitives. Among them, memristors, as the most experimentally mature devices, have demonstrated significant potential in Physical Unclonable Functions (PUFs) and True Random Number Generators (TRNGs) by exploiting their intrinsic variability, nonlinearity, and history-dependent behavior. By contrast, memcapacitors and meminductors, which extend memory effects to energy-storing electrical and magnetic domains, remain largely unexplored in security applications, despite their richer dynamical structure and greater theoretical potential for entropy generation and resistance to inference. This mini-review provides a structured overview of the state of the art of mem-elements in hardware security, highlighting the differences in dynamical behavior and security-relevant properties across memristors, memcapacitors, and meminductors. The review identifies key limitations of current approaches based on static or low-dimensional variability, discusses the implications of machine-learning-based modelling attacks, and outlines open research challenges associated with the limited availability of memcapacitive and meminductive devices. Finally, it explores the potential of coupled memcapacitor–meminductor systems as a fundamentally new platform for entropy-driven and dynamically evolving security primitives, opening promising directions for next-generation hardware security.
articles.summary_en: A review compares memristors, memcapacitors and meminductors as hardware-security primitives, including physical unclonable functions and true random-number generators. It highlights machine-learning attack risks and proposes coupled memcapacitor–meminductor systems as a future entropy-generation platform.

articles.title_original: Nonlinear Conductive Behavior of 2D-Selenido Stannates
articles.title_en: 2D Selenido Stannates Show Structure-Dependent Nonlinear Conductivity
articles.excerpt_original: Chalcogenido metalates have long been regarded as cluster-based semiconductors, yet their conductive nature has not been studied in detail, although such compounds do bear potential for use in electronics. Herein, we introduce four new compounds, (HDMMP)$_2$[Sn$_3$Se$_7$]·(HDMMP)$_2$[Sn$_2$Se$_6$]$_{0.5}$ (1), (C$_3$C$_1$Im)$_3$(HDMMP)[Sn$_3$Se$_7$]$_2$ (2), and their Cs$^+$-exchanged derivatives, 1$^{Cs}$ and 2$^{Cs}$ (HDMMP = protonated 2,6-dimethylmorpholine; C$_3$C$_1$Im = 1-propyl-3-methyl-imidazolium), all of which are based on 2D-{[Sn$_3$Se$_7$]$^{2–}$} anionic substructures. Detailed current–voltage measurements on single crystals of 1 and 2 as well as their ion-exchanged derivatives were undertaken that indicated complex nonlinear and highly structure-dependent conductive properties. For 1, the studies demonstrate that intercalation of molecular 0D-[Sn$_2$Se$_6$]$^{4–}$ units with higher negative charge density as compared to the 2D-{[Sn$_3$Se$_7$]$^{2–}$} networks creates open circuits that lead to nonconductive characteristics. In contrast, the I–V measurements carried out on 2 suggest a combination of electrical and ionic conductivity along horizontal and vertical directions of this compound based exclusively on the 2D-{[Sn$_3$Se$_7$]$^{2–}$} substructures. Cation exchange in 1 and 2 with Cs$^+$, which in the case of compound 1 is accompanied by an extraction of the molecular anions 0D-[Sn$_2$Se$_6$]$^{4–}$, confirms this suggestion: a set of I–V characteristics, including I–V hysteresis and chronoamperometry traces, demonstrate that both compounds are now conductive, with ionic conductivity dominating along both vertical and horizontal directions of 1$^{Cs}$ and 2$^{Cs}$. Notably, compound 1 not only turned into a conductive material 1$^{Cs}$, it additional
articles.summary_en: Researchers synthesized four 2D selenido stannate compounds and measured strongly structure-dependent electrical and ionic conductivity. Cesium exchange transformed otherwise nonconductive or weakly conductive structures into materials dominated by ionic transport, indicating potential relevance to electronic and ionic-device research.

articles.title_original: Relativistic quantum antiscars in electrostatically defined graphene quantum dots
articles.title_en: Relativistic Quantum Antiscars in Graphene Quantum Dots
articles.summary_en: Researchers report theoretical relativistic quantum antiscars in electrostatically defined graphene quantum dots. The work advances fundamental understanding of quantum behavior in graphene nanostructures, with potential relevance to future semiconductor research.

articles.title_original: Long-Lifespan Turbostratic Graphene Field Emitters for High-Power Applications
articles.title_en: Turbostratic Graphene Field Emitters Sustain High-Power Operation for 588 Hours
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract Cold cathodes offer heater-free, instantly switchable electron sources, but conventional sharp-tip designs often degrade under continuous thermal loads, limiting high-power applications. We overcome this with a freestanding, edge-emitting turbostratic graphene film (GF). Its turbostratic stacked layers are assembled via solution-phase pre-gelation of graphene oxide, followed by thermal restoration and densification. A 300 nm-thick, 1 cm-wide GF emission edge can sustain 1.5 mA (52 A cm–2) DC current for 588 h, with an exceptionally low degradation rate below 0.042% h–1. This durability is an order of magnitude better than previous carbon cathodes at similar current densities. This performance meets critical requirements for modern high-power vacuum electron applications. Our cost-effective, scalable architecture bridges nanoscopic field enhancement with macroscopic heat management, significantly broadening cold cathode applications.
articles.summary_en: Researchers developed a freestanding turbostratic graphene film cold cathode that sustained 1.5 mA DC emission for 588 hours with degradation below 0.042% per hour. The scalable architecture combines field emission with heat management, supporting potential high-power vacuum-electron applications.

articles.title_original: Mesoscopic interferences in transport through Ti <sub>3</sub> C <sub>2</sub> T <sub>x</sub> MXene flakes
articles.title_en: MXene flakes show mesoscopic interference in charge transport
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract Charge transport in MXenes is often studied in disordered films, with the perspective of their applications in energy storage, EMI shielding or sensors, among others. In this configuration, interflake coupling prevents isolating the fundamental properties of individual flakes, whose properties have been scarcely studied. Here, we investigate transport at the mesoscopic scale, combining temperature- and magneticfield-dependent measurements on isolated flakes and interflake junctions of the prototypical MXene Ti 3 C 2 T x . Both configurations exhibit metallic behavior with a low temperature logarithmic correction to the conductance consistent with weak localization (WL) in two dimensions, and an enhanced disorder associated with interflake coupling. Magnetoconductance measurements reveal clear signatures of mesoscopic interferences in the form of WL, analyzed quantitatively within the Hikami-Larkin-Nagaoka model, and reproducible Universal Conductance Fluctuations.
articles.summary_en: IOP Publishing researchers measured temperature- and magnetic-field-dependent transport in isolated Ti₃C₂Tₓ MXene flakes and interflake junctions. The findings reveal weak localization and reproducible universal conductance fluctuations, offering fundamental insight relevant to MXene-based energy-storage and sensor devices.

articles.title_original: Green synthesis of graphene oxide via electrochemical exfoliation and its characterization
articles.title_en: Electrochemical Exfoliation Produces Lower-Defect Graphene Oxide
articles.excerpt_original: Graphene oxide (GO) is a versatile carbon nanomaterial whose properties strongly depend on the synthesis route. In this study, an environmentally friendly electrochemical exfoliation (EE) method using 0.1 M ammonium sulfate electrolyte was developed and compared with the conventional Hummers' method (HM). The influence of electrolysis duration and purification on the structural and electrical properties of the obtained materials was systemically investigated. UV–Vis spectroscopy showed a characteristic absorption band at approximately 190 nm for electrochemically exfoliated samples, while prolonged electrolysis (8 h) resulted in the appearance of a weak shoulder near 230 nm, indicating gradual oxidation of the graphite structure. XRD analysis revealed that HM-derived GO exhibited a characteristic (001) reflection at 11.09° (d-spacing = 7.99 Å), whereas electrochemically exfoliated GO retained a broad (002) peak centered at 26.54°, corresponding to an interlayer spacing of 3.36 Å and indicating partial preservation of the graphitic structure. Raman spectroscopy demonstrated a lower defect density in electrochemically exfoliated GO, with an I D /I G ratio of 0.759 compared with 0.864 for HM-derived GO. FTIR spectra further confirmed the lower abundance of oxygen-containing functional groups in the electrochemically synthesized material. Electron microscopy revealed thin, transparent, wrinkled graphene-like nanosheets with significantly improved exfoliation after dialysis. Electrical resistivity measurements performed between 40 and 100 °C under laboratory air, humid atmosphere, and flowing argon demonstrated consistently lower resistivity for electrochemically exfoliated GO than for HM-derived GO, indicating higher electrical conductivity due to its lower oxidation degree
articles.summary_en: Researchers developed a greener electrochemical exfoliation method using ammonium sulfate and compared it with the Hummers method. The electrochemically produced graphene oxide showed lower oxidation and defect levels, better preservation of graphitic structure, and lower resistivity under tested conditions.

articles.title_original: Janus Al 2 Si 2 X 3 Y 3 ( X/Y = S, Se, Te) monolayers: A first-principles investigation of structural, electronic, optical, and transport properties
articles.title_en: Janus Al₂Si₂X₃Y₃ Monolayers Show Promise for Optoelectronics
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract First-principles calculations were performed to investigate Janus Al$_2$Si$_2$X$_3$Y$_3$ ($X/Y$ = S, Se, Te) monolayers as two-dimensional semiconductors for optoelectronic applications. Phonon spectra, \textit{ab initio} molecular dynamics at 300 K, and elastic constants confirm their dynamical, thermal, and mechanical stability. The lattice constant and thickness increase from 6.10 to 6.56 \AA\ and from 3.19 to 3.42 \AA, respectively, whereas the in-plane Young's modulus decreases from 92.70 to 75.13 N m$^{-1}$ with heavier chalcogen substitution. All three monolayers are semiconductors with HSE06 band gaps of 3.15, 1.26, and 1.67 eV for Al$_2$Si$_2$S$_3$Se$_3$, Al$_2$Si$_2$S$_3$Te$_3$, and Al$_2$Si$_2$Se$_3$Te$_3$, respectively. Janus asymmetry induces intrinsic electrostatic polarity with side-dependent work-function differences of 0.18--0.46 eV. The Te-containing systems show broader optical absorption, with coefficients on the order of $10^{5}$. Carrier-transport calculations reveal nearly isotropic in-plane behavior and pronounced electron-dominated mobility, reaching 1654.03 cm$^{2}$ V$^{-1}$ s$^{-1}$ in Al$_2$Si$_2$Se$_3$Te$_3$. These results identify Janus Al$_2$Si$_2$X$_3$Y$_3$ monolayers as promising candidates for multifunctional nanoelectronic and optoelectronic devices.
articles.summary_en: First-principles calculations indicate that Janus Al₂Si₂X₃Y₃ monolayers are stable semiconductors with tunable band gaps, polarity, optical absorption, and electron mobility. The findings support their potential for multifunctional nanoelectronic and optoelectronic devices, but remain computational rather than experimentally validated.

articles.title_original: Patent Landscape Review of MXene Composites for Advanced Functional Materials
articles.title_en: Patent Landscape Review Maps 658 MXene Composite Families
articles.excerpt_original: MXene composites represent an exceptionally promising member of the family of two-dimensional multifunctional materials known for outstanding electrical properties, mechanical strength, chemical tuning abilities, and the potential for wide applications. The paper conducts a profound patent landscape investigation of MXene composites with the help of the WIPO PATENTSCOPE database. In total, 658 patent families were found; duplicate patent entries were eliminated through the application of the Single Family Member method. The results show that China is a patent leader worldwide, followed by PCT applications and the patenting activity of the USA, India, and other countries, which indicates a growing international interest in MXene technologies and materials. The classification of patents also shows that this technology is actively researched in relation to the development of technologies in the field of electrochemical energy storage, polymer engineering, sensing technologies, catalysis, environmental remediation, electronics, and biomedical applications. Additionally, the paper studies the technology development in the field of the creation of MXene antennas, semiconductor devices, and ceramic oxide composites, materials that change shape, anti-corrosion coatings, electrochemical sensors, and many others. Even though substantial advances have been made, obstacles related to efficient manufacturing, oxidation resistance, quality assurance, sustainability, and industry adoption persist. The overall picture of patents shows that MXene-based composite materials have progressed from the testing stage to commercial products with high potential for next-generation technologies.
articles.summary_en: An academic review identified 658 MXene-composite patent families, led by China and followed by PCT, US, and Indian filings. The patents span energy storage, sensing, environmental remediation, electronics, biomedical applications, coatings, and semiconductor technologies, while manufacturing and commercialization challenges remain.

articles.title_original: A 3D MXene–CNT–Ag SERS platform with high enhancement and uniformity for quantitative analysis of complex botanical extracts
articles.title_en: 3D MXene–CNT–Ag SERS Platform Enables Quantitative Analysis of Botanical Extracts
articles.summary_en: Researchers developed a three-dimensional MXene–carbon nanotube–silver surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy platform designed to improve signal enhancement and uniformity. The system supports quantitative analysis of complex botanical extracts, indicating potential for analytical sensing applications.

articles.title_original: Gradient-based optimization of non-Abelian fractional quantum states in patterned superlattices
articles.title_en: Gradient Optimization Targets Non-Abelian States in Bilayer Graphene Superlattices
articles.excerpt_original: The realization of fractional Chern insulator (FCI) states in moiré heterostructures has attracted intense interest in the study of correlated states emerging from topological flat bands. So far, most experimentally realized FCI states may be interpreted as lattice analogues of fractional quantum Hall (FQH) states hosting Abelian anyonic excitations. Realizing non-Abelian FCI states is an important challenge in the field. Patterned dielectric superlattices provide a versatile platform for engineering topological flat bands. Such systems offer substantial structural flexibility and tunability, because their lattice patterns, periods, and other structural parameters can all be designed and fabricated. Here we propose to realize non-Abelian FCI states in patterned dielectric superlattices coupled to bilayer graphene. Specifically, we provide a realistic workflow based on a gradient-descent algorithm to design non-Abelian fractional states in bilayer graphene superlattices. The experimentally relevant structural parameters of the superlattices are gradient-optimized to favor a flat Chern band with quantum-geometric properties reminiscent of those of the first excited Landau level. Exact diagonalization calculations at 1/2 filling of the optimized flat Chern band naturally yield non-Abelian FCI states. We apply this workflow to triangular, honeycomb, and kagome patterned superlattices and find robust non-Abelian FCI states over a large region of the parameter space spanned by the superlattice constant and vertical potential drop. Our work thus establishes an experimentally feasible framework for exploring non-Abelian FCIs in realistic patterned-superlattice devices. It also demonstrates the potential of device-level inverse design to engineer correlated topological matter be
articles.summary_en: Researchers propose a gradient-descent workflow to design patterned dielectric superlattices supporting non-Abelian fractional Chern insulator states in bilayer graphene. Simulations across triangular, honeycomb, and kagome patterns indicate robust states over broad structural parameter ranges, offering a theoretical path toward engineered topological devices.

articles.title_original: A comprehensive review on synthesis, properties, and pest control applications of two-dimensional graphene-based materials

articles.title_original: Synthesis and characterization of tungsten disulfide-graphene oxide nanocomposite
articles.title_en: Researchers Synthesize Tungsten Disulfide–Graphene Oxide Nanocomposite
articles.excerpt_original: Two-dimensional (2D) materials, such as tungsten disulfide (WS 2 ) and graphene oxide (GO), have garnered significant attention. This is due to their unique physicochemical properties and potential applications in catalysis, electronics, and phototherapy. In this study, we report the synthesis and characterization of WS 2 nanosheets, GO nanosheets, and a novel WS 2 -GO nanocomposite (NC). The NC was prepared via a simple wet-chemical method, which is low-cost and versatile, ensuring uniform dispersion and strong interfacial interactions between the WS 2 and GO nanosheets. Functional group identification was done by Fourier Transform Infrared Spectroscopy (FT-IR), while structural and morphological analysis was done using X-Ray Diffraction (XRD), Field Emission Scanning Electron Microscopy (FE-SEM), and Transmission Electron Microscopy (TEM). Additionally, Energy Dispersive X-ray Spectroscopy (EDX) verified a homogeneous elemental distribution. FT-IR spectra of the NC reveal characteristic bands for carboxyl, hydroxyl, and alkoxy groups from GO, as well as W-S and S-S vibrational modes from WS 2 . XRD analysis confirms the crystalline nature of WS 2 -GO NC, displaying the characteristic GO peak alongside distinct diffraction peaks corresponding to the hexagonal phase of WS 2 , which verifies the successful formation of the hybrid. SEM and TEM imaging visually confirm the integration of WS 2 onto the wrinkled GO surface with minimal aggregation and high crystallinity, as supported by selected area electron diffraction (SAED). articles.title_original: All-Electron Single-Atom Reference Correction for Absolute Transition Energies in Fixed-Reference PAW-XCH Calculations
articles.title_en: All-Electron Corrections Improve Absolute Core-Loss Energy Predictions
articles.excerpt_original: The transition energy of a core-loss spectrum comprises a transferable atomic core-reference contribution and a material-dependent response that determines chemical shifts. Density functional theory calculations commonly underestimate absolute transition energies. In VASP, the same PAW dataset is used for the ground and core-excited occupations, retaining the ground-state atomic reference when the core occupation changes and thereby omitting the associated all-electron atomic reference change. We evaluate this change using self-consistent single-atom calculations and construct a residual atomic reference correction from the valence reference change and isolated-atom total-energy response. Comparisons with an independent ultrasoft-pseudopotential implementation demonstrate numerical consistency of the all-electron reference for K, L1, and L2,3 core holes, while representative corrected spectra approach the experimental absolute energy scale. For a fixed element, edge, and core-hole scheme, the atomic reference terms cancel from energy differences, showing that same-element chemical shifts are governed by the double difference of the supercell total energy. At the Al and Si L2,3 edges, the near-edge spectral shape additionally depends strongly on the PAW representation of low-lying 3d-like unoccupied states.
articles.summary_en: Researchers developed an atomic reference correction for fixed-reference PAW-XCH calculations, improving agreement between computed and experimental absolute transition energies. The study also shows that same-element chemical shifts depend on supercell energy differences, while PAW representation affects near-edge spectral shapes at aluminum and silicon edges.

articles.title_original: Preserved metallicity and tunable magnetism in Zr-based Janus MXenes
articles.title_en: Zr-Based Janus MXenes Preserve Metallic Behavior and Enable Tunable Magnetism
articles.excerpt_original: Janus MXenes provide a chemically asymmetric platform to tailor the properties of two-dimensional transition metal carbides. Here, we present a systematic first-principles study of the structural, electronic, mechanical, and magnetic properties of Janus ZrMCX2 MXenes (M = Cr, Hf, Nb, Sc, Ti; X = F, Cl, S). All compositions exhibit negative formation energies and satisfy the Born stability criteria, supporting the energetic and mechanical stability of the Janus structures. In contrast to the metal-tosemiconductor transitions frequently reported for functionalized MXenes, we find that the metallic character is preserved in nearly all ZrMCX2 systems, despite the strong chemical asymmetry introduced by the Janus configuration. Surface functionalization nevertheless plays a key role in modulating the electronic density near the Fermi level and strongly influences the magnetic and mechanical responses. Several compounds exhibit ferromagnetic or antiferromagnetic ground states, three display halfmetallicity, and sizable magnetic anisotropy energies are obtained, with Neel temperatures exceeding room temperature in selected cases. Functionalization also enhances the elastic stiffness of the Janus structures. These results demonstrate that chemical asymmetry and surface termination provide effective control over magnetic and mechanical properties while maintaining a robust metallic framework, identifying Zr-based Janus MXenes as promising model systems for metallic and spindependent two-dimensional materials.
articles.summary_en: A first-principles study finds that most Janus ZrMCX2 MXenes remain metallic despite chemical asymmetry, while surface functionalization tunes their electronic, magnetic, and mechanical properties. Several compositions show ferro- or antiferromagnetism, half-metallicity, and potentially room-temperature magnetic ordering, positioning them as model two-dimensional materials for spin-dependent applications.

bulletin.title: Graphene Weekly Bulletin — Week ending 2026-08-16
bulletin.introduction: This week’s evidence points to graphene innovation concentrating on engineered interfaces and composite architectures, spanning thermal management, flame retardancy, structural reinforcement, coatings and flexible electronics. Research repeatedly indicates that dispersion, layer design and processing routes govern performance, while several patents seek to translate these approaches into application-specific materials. Commercial activity is emerging in additive-manufacturing filaments and supply capacity, alongside consolidation and financing, but disclosed deployment scale and economics remain limited. Advanced electronic and quantum studies continue to broaden longer-term option value.
